title: Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot
text:
Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot

['From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@finlytic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot

Hi Sophie —

Great to meet you and Tomas on the call today. Quick recap and the two asks we discussed so Redwood can put a clean pilot proposal together:

1) Volume profile (you said rough ranges on the call): please confirm monthly token range and expected peak bursts (tokens/month and tokens/minute). You mentioned mainly inference for NER and summarization; we used 50–70 tokens per call as a baseline.
2) Target unit economics: what is your finance/ops target $ per 1M tokens for production? If you have a preferred range we should use for quoting.

High-level notes from our side re: US vs EU hosting and cost drivers: 
- Baseline hosted US price (ballpark): $1,000 per 1M tokens for the model family we discussed (chat + long-context summarization).
- EU hosting typically carries a 15–25% regional premium driven by higher infra spot price in some EU zones, additional egress/transfer dynamics, and extra compliance/ops hardening for data locality. For your profile I’d model a ~20% uplift (so roughly $1,200 / 1M tokens) for EU-hosted single-tenant workloads.
- Other unit cost levers: batching, KV prefix caching, quantized model variants — these can lower effective $/1M by 10–40% depending on request shape.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You confirm the two items above (volumes and target $/1M).
- I’ll share a short pricing worksheet (attached) with three scenarios: US-hosted, EU-hosted, and EU-hosted + dedicated pool. Each scenario will include expected latency SLO, estimated monthly spend, and a rough timeline for provisioning.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (ballpark math), SOW template (procurement-ready).

If easier, we can run a quick 15-min session with Ben (pricing lead) to walk the worksheet live.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0198

', 'From: Sophie Martin <sophie@finlytic.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomas Varga <tomas.varga@finlytic.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 17:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot

Thanks Evelyn — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: current pilot scope is conservative — 2M to 6M tokens / month initially, with a goal to ramp to ~20M tokens/mo over 6–9 months if latency and accuracy meet SLAs. Peak bursts up to ~5k requests/min. Average token per request ~60.
- Target unit economics: our finance team is modeling an internal target of ~$1,100 per 1M tokens for vendor costs in EU (they quoted this as a hard threshold for the pilot budget). If you can get closer to $900–1,000 / 1M in US, that would be interesting — but note we cannot host customer data outside the EU for production without additional approvals.
- Procurement timeline: best case — PO in Jan, pilot in Feb, production by May if all goes well. We will need SOC 2 + dataflow diagram + DPA.

Can you return the worksheet with EU and US columns and a row showing the incremental delta (EUR premium)? Also include any one-time provisioning fees for dedicated pools.

Cheers,
Sophie
Head of Product
Finlytic

', 'From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@finlytic.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the clarity. Quick answers / commitments from our side: 

- We’ll return a pricing worksheet with three rows: Hosted US (multi-tenant), Hosted EU (multi-tenant, data-resident), and Dedicated EU pool (reserved). Each will show: price per 1M tokens, expected monthly range, estimated latency SLO, and the one-time provisioning charge (if any).
- For the pilot profile you described (2–6M tokens/mo), baseline ballpark numbers (subject to model selection & batching):
  • Hosted US: $950 / 1M tokens
  • Hosted EU: $1,140 / 1M tokens (20% premium)
  • Dedicated EU pool (monthly reserved capacity, starting tier): $950 / 1M tokens effective at >25M tokens/mo but includes a $6k/mo commitment + provisioning (useful once you ramp).

- Caching & batching: with a 60-token average and standard batching we expect to drive 15–25% savings vs the raw baseline in production. We’ll model conservative and optimistic delta rows.

Next steps: Evelyn will upload the worksheet with line-item math and we’ll schedule a 20-min review with your procurement on Friday (if that works). Procurement docs we’ll attach: SOC 2 report stub, DPA template, and a high-level data flow diagram.

— Ben
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

', 'From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@finlytic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot

Sophie / Tomas —

Uploading the worksheet now (attached). A few callouts from the math sheet:

- The EU premium in the sheet is calculated as: regional infra margin (~8%), additional ops & replication (~6%), and DR/availability SLAs (~6%) — totaling ~20% on the hosted SKU.
- We included a worked example for a 3-month pilot at 4M tokens/mo:
  • Hosted EU (multi-tenant): $1,140 / 1M -> est monthly vendor cost $4,560
  • Hosted US (multi-tenant): $950 / 1M -> est monthly vendor cost $3,800 (not production-viable for you due to data-location)
  • Dedicated EU reserved (small tier): effective $980 / 1M once combined with a $6k/mo commitment — shows value as you approach sustained 25M/mo.

- One-time provisioning: dedicated pool requires a 2–4 week provisioning window and a one-time setup of $4,000 for network/VPC onboarding (we show that as amortized in the worksheet).

Suggested immediate next actions:
1) Confirm you received the worksheet and whether the $1,140 / 1M EU baseline is within the acceptable range for procurement to build a PO.
2) If yes, we’ll schedule the Friday review with finance/procurement and attach SOC 2 + DPA.

I’ve attached: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx and our SOW template (for procurement).

— Evelyn

', 'From: Tomas Varga <tomas.varga@finlytic.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie@finlytic.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing sensitivity & data-location impact for Finlytic pilot

Evelyn / Ben —

Received the worksheet — thanks. Quick confirmation from procurement side: the $1,140 / 1M EU baseline is close to what we expected. We need the following before we can issue a PO:
- Signed DPA (we’ll send our redline)
- SOC 2 Type II report (recent) and an architecture/dataflow slide showing where tokens/keys live (we need to validate no outbound PII flows outside EU).
- A line in the SOW that confirms rollback/fallback policy: if performance regresses >20% vs baseline during pilot, we can pause and re-evaluate without penalty.

If you can provide those by COB Monday we’ll go to legal and procurement and aim to get a PO in mid-Jan. Also please include an explicit row in the worksheet showing per-1M effective price after 20% optimistic caching savings — procurement likes to see best-case/worst-case.

Thanks — Tomas
Head of IT Ops | Finlytic
']
